title: In vitro phosphoproteomic analysis of neonatal rat cardiac myocytes
protocol: Warm 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA in a 37°C water bath.
Warm 10% FBS, 1% penicillin streptomycin supplemented DMEM in a 37°C water bath.
Spray the sterile biosafety cabinet with 75% ethanol prior to entering.
Gather warmed trypsin and media in the sterile biosafety cabinet.
Gather cold PBS in the sterile biosafety cabinet.
Prepare pipetman and pipette tips for use in the sterile biosafety cabinet.
Collect 1.7 ml and 15 ml tubes for use in the sterile biosafety cabinet.
Collect a small waste container near the sterile biosafety cabinet.
Place vacuum nearby the sterile biosafety cabinet.
Position a liquid nitrogen-containing container nearby the sterile biosafety cabinet.
Place a refrigerated centrifuge nearby.
Gently remove existing media from RNCM culture plates, leaving cell monolayer attached to the plate.
Add 1 ml of 0.25% trypsin to each well for RNCM culture plates.
Avoid letting cells sit in trypsin for more than 1-2 minutes.
Use additional trypsin if needed to detach cells within a timely manner.
Rock, swirl, or tap the plate only if absolutely necessary to detach cells from the plate.
Add 2 ml of 10% FBS, 1% penicillin streptomycin supplemented DMEM to stop trypsin action and place cells in suspension.
Collect suspended RNCM cells and media into 15 ml round bottom tubes by pooling at least three wells together.
Centrifuge the collected cells at 1,200 rpm for 2 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully decant the media into a small waste container, leaving cell pellet at the bottom of the tube.
Remove any remaining media by turning tube upside down.
Do NOT use vacuum to remove media.
Add 1 ml cold PBS, re-suspend pellet with pipette, and transfer to a 1.7 ml tube.
Centrifuge at 1,200 rpm for 2 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully decant PBS into small waste container leaving cell pellet at bottom.
Remove any remaining PBS by turning tube upside down.
Do NOT vacuum to remove PBS.
Repeat PBS wash an additional 1-2 times to ensure removal of media.
Flash freeze pellet in liquid nitrogen.
Store at -80°C until ready for phosphoproteome analysis.
Lysate samples in 200 µL of 8M Urea, 0.5% SDS with brief sonication and determine protein concentration by the BCA method.
Incubate 200 µg of total protein in a solution containing 50 mM NH4HCO3 pH 8, 1.3 M Urea, 0.08% SDS, 11 mM fresh DTT at room temperature for 1 hr.
Treat samples with 108 µL of 200 mM iodoacetamide and incubate at room temperature for 1 hr in the dark.
Treat samples with 20 µg of trypsin/Lys-C protease mixture.
Incubate the sample overnight for 18-24 hours at 37°C with shaking.
Stop the reaction by adding 100 μL of 10% TFA to drop the pH below 2.
Desalt samples on Oasis HLB cartridges.
Elute desalted samples in 300 µL of 80% ACN, 5% TFA, and 1 M glycolic acid.
Treat eluted samples with 50 μL of TiO2 slurry (30 mg/mL).
Incubate the TiO2-treated samples overnight at room temperature or 25°C.
Wash TiO2 beads three times with 200 µL of 80% ACN, 5% TFA.
Wash TiO2 beads once with 200 μL of 80% ACN and 0.1% TFA.
Elute phosphopeptides with 200 μL of 1% NH4OH.
Acidify eluted samples with 50 µL of 10% TFA.
Desalt acidified samples on Oasis HLB µ-elution plates.
Elute desalted samples in 200 µL of 80% ACN and 0.1% FA.
Dry the eluted samples under vacuum.
Resuspend dried peptides in 10-20 μL of 0.1% formic acid (FA).
Inject phosphopeptides onto an EASY-nLC 1000 system.
Perform LC-MS/MS analysis using a Q-Exactive Plus equipped with a nano-electrospray ion source.
Load peptides onto a Dionex Acclaim® PepMap100 trap column \(Thermo, 75 µm x 2 cm, C18 3 µm 100Å).
Separate peptides on a Dionex Acclaim® PepMap RSLC analytical column \(Thermo, 50 µm x 15 cm, C18 2 µm 100Å) at a flow rate of 300 nL/min.
Apply a linear gradient of 0-30% B for 90 minutes.
Increase the gradient to 30-95% B for 5 minutes.
Hold at 95% B for 1 minute.
Set the nano-source capillary temperature to 275 °C.
Set the spray voltage to 2 kV.
Acquire MS1 scans at a resolution of 70,000 full width at half maximum \(FWHM) with an AGC target of 1e6 and a maximum accumulation time of 250 ms.
Select the top 15 ions in each MS1 scan for fragmentation using normalized collision energy of 30% with an isolation window of 2 Da.
Acquire MS2 scans at a resolution of 17,500 FWHM with an AGC target of 5e5 and a maximum fill time of 150 ms.
Search raw files against an appropriate peptide database using an appropriate search algorithm.
Select trypsin as the digesting enzyme.
Set carbamidomethyl as a fixed modification on Cys.
Specify variable modifications of oxidation on Met and phosphorylation on Ser, Thr, and Tyr.
Perform post-search analysis using Scaffold 4 with protein and peptide probability thresholds set to 95% and 90%, respectively.
Require one peptide for identification.
Determine phosphosite localization using Scaffold PTM version 2.1.3.
Ignore phosphosites with probabilities less than 90%.
Carry out manual validation for ambiguously assigned phosphosites.
Use computational algorithms and methods to score the confidence of the phosphosite assignment.
